title: The Savior Hides His Face
description: The Savior Hides His Face in Tonic Solfa to BOYLSTON, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 7 verses and a piano.
about: William Cowper wrote these words. They were printed in Olney Hymns (London, 1779), Book III, hymn 24, “Mourning and longing”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Short Metre (6.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to BOYLSTON; any other Short Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: The Sa-vior hides his face! My spir-it thirsts to prove Re-newed sup-plies of pard'n-ing grace, And nev-er fa-ding love.

lines: Pant for his presence, as the roe
They cleave to everything I do,
How toilsome then to sing and pray,
Of all the truths I hear
I glean a berry here and there,
No pleasure else is worth a thought,
Though I am but a worm,
The Lord will my desire perform,
And grant me all my prayer.

source: John Newton and William Cowper, Olney Hymns (1779)
licence: Public domain: William Cowper died in 1800.
credits: Words by William Cowper (1731–1800), public domain, as printed in Olney Hymns (1779); set to BOYLSTON by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
